title: fix(run): warn on stderr when a self-linked dist is older than its src
description:
## .what

in a repo that links its own build into .agent (a role package that dogfoods its skills), rhx resolves each skill through dist/**/*.js, never src/. no step warns when dist is older than src, so a live skill call runs the previous build in silence.

checkable evidence, from ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhrain on 2026-09-04:
- dist/domain.operations/route/guard/review/peer/ still held getAllRouteGuardReviewPeerGivensAtHash.js, which src had deleted
- dist lacked getLatestPeerGivensPerSlug.js, which src had added
- four live rhx route.stone.set calls answered from the pre-fix engine, plausibly and with no error, while types/unit/format/lint (all of which read src) were green

## .why

the stale engine does not fail; it answers in the shape the caller expects. in a repo whose product is a guard, the reviewer, the gate, and the halt are all the previous version, on the very branch meant to change them. no test catches it, since the test suites compile src.

## .shape of the fix

1. at skill resolution (findUniqueSkillExecutable or the rhx entrypoint), when the resolved executable sits under a dist/ whose package root also holds a src/, compare the newest src/**/*.ts mtime against the newest dist/**/*.js mtime
2. if src is newer, warn on stderr and continue, for example:
   ⚠️ dist is older than src, so this ran the PREVIOUS build. fix: npm run build
3. warn, never halt: a stale dist is normal mid-edit, and a hard stop would break every skill call in ordinary work. an mtime compare is a heuristic (a touched file yields a false warn), which is acceptable for a warn and not for a gate
4. clamp: a fixture package with src newer than dist asserts the warn on stderr; equal mtimes assert silence

a build step inside the skill path was considered and rejected: it slows every call and couples the runner to the build.
